blocks.x: Thirty minutes, same time every week. This is what stops the package becoming a folder you bought and stopped opening. Adoption without a standing review decays in about three weeks — not because people object to it, but because nothing brings it back to attention.
Record these every week. Four weeks of real numbers is worth more than any estimate of time saved.

head: Measure
This week
Last week
Direction
rows: Notes returned to technicians for clarification
Average days from job completion to invoice
Customers who received a post-job summary (%)

x: Which prompt earned its place this week
Who used it and for what
Anything worth telling the rest of the team

blocks.x: This is the part that matters. Be specific — "the AI was unhelpful" cannot be fixed; "the estimate prompt keeps leaving out our disposal exclusion" can be fixed in two minutes.
Pick two customer-facing documents sent this week at random. Run them through the Quality-Control Checklist now, together.

x: Document 1 — passed / failed, and on which item
Document 2 — passed / failed, and on which item

blocks.x: If the same checklist item fails twice in a month, the problem is the prompt or the training, not the person. Fix the upstream cause.

x: Who is doing what by when
Read three SOPs written more than a month ago. Are they still accurate? Procedures drift and nobody notices until a new hire follows the old one.
Check that new staff have signed the Responsible Use acknowledgement.
Review whether any prohibited use has crept in — particularly pricing and anything customer-facing going out unreviewed.
Ask: what are we still doing manually that we said we would change?

blocks.x: Keep the completed forms. Twelve weeks of these is the clearest record you will have of whether this actually changed anything.
